In B, 'for all drinkware on' is set nearly as large as the price, so it competes with it, and it almost touches the stripe graphic. A keeps a gap there and a clearer price-first hierarchy, so it is marginally better.

Both break up the original: the full-height colour stripes shrink to three small decorative bars and the white card is lost. 'for all drinkware on', which explains the price, drops to an unreadable speck. In both, the vertical URL floats in the middle of large dead white gaps. A also has a smallish price and a small, cramped product list in the far-right corner, with the caption shrunk to illegible size at the bottom. B gives the price and the list more presence and fills the height better, but its caption is even smaller (invisible) and the list is jammed against the right edge, so B is only the less bad of the two.

A and B look pixel-identical. Both squeeze the invitation copy into a narrow column of one or two words per line ('THIS / SUMMER / IN / LIVONIA'), which is hard to read. The dates are stacked into a cramped, ragged column, and the cross is blown up and blurry, so it competes with the headline. 'WORSHIP & BIBLE STUDY' is tiny and isolated at the bottom. The mountain and hiker illustration is cut off with a hard bottom edge and floats in the right corner, and there is dead space beneath the headline.

A: the cat illustration should bleed off the bottom edge as in the original, but here it stops in a hard flat line about 96px above the bottom, leaving a strip of purple underneath. The headline also runs almost to the side edges, and there is unused space above it. B has the same problem, only worse: the illustration is smaller and floats above a large empty purple area of about 165px, so the cut edge stands out even more. The cats look shrunken and lose their impact, and the layout is badly bottom-heavy with empty space.

A has three different left edges: the headline is at about x=22, the blue info box at about x=30 and the black box at about x=50. The black box is also narrower and floats off-centre, so the stack looks staggered and arbitrary, and the gaps between the blocks are uneven. B lines both boxes up as full-width panels on the same margin as the headline and sets the black box's copy at a readable size, so the column reads clean. B's flaws, which A shares: 'COPENHAGEN' runs almost to the right edge, the background photo is cropped to a vague washed-out wall that loses the furniture imagery, and the headline's 5-line stack sits right on top of the blue box.

A and B are pixel-identical. In both, the stained-glass window is stretched wider than its original proportions (the arch looks squat and the cross bar runs past the right edge of the window). The window fills most of the canvas and dwarfs the headline. The date and address are tiny, oddly offset from each other (the date is indented and the address is flush left) and crammed under the window with almost no gap. The whole block is shifted left, leaving the right margin uneven.

A breaks the design: the three small crosses are blown up into huge, blurry white bars across the face, the cloud shapes are stretched into a disjointed white blob over the image, and the quote is crammed into a bottom box with 'MAHATMA GANDHI' moved beside it as a competing column. B keeps the original composition, crosses and type intact, but it is basically a scaled copy with black side bars and the cloud band not reaching the canvas edges (with a strip of photo showing at the left and right), so it needs edge cleanup before it could ship.

Both break the design the same way. The S-A-L-E letters have been pulled out of their circles: the circles sit as an empty white stack in the middle, the letters are scattered across the banner, and the small 'L' is jammed against the 'E'. The lanterns and clouds are shrunk into illegible clusters, so the word SALE no longer reads. The only difference is that A's headline is slightly larger and closer to the left edge, while B's is a bit smaller with a little more margin. Neither difference matters next to the shared breakage.

Both lose the original's full-height stripe background. They shrink it to three small bars and scatter the price, the vertical URL and the product list across empty white space, and the 'for all drinkware on' line is shrunk to illegible micro-text. That line sits right under the list in A and floats alone at the bottom in B. A is less bad because its price and list are large, fill the height and read clearly. B's list is small and floats in a large dead area, and its sideways URL now outweighs the list.

A and B look pixel-identical, so this is a tie. Both stack the design sensibly but share the same flaws: the stained-glass window takes up most of the canvas and dwarfs the headline, which is small for the format. The date line sits off-centre and doesn't line up with the left-aligned address beneath it. The date and address are small and cramped at the bottom, while there are wide empty margins on the right and left.

Both have broken hierarchy: the supporting line 'with your next cup of coffee' is far bigger than the 'GET A GIFT' headline. In both, the gift icons, oversized stars, 'Only this Christmas' and the URL sit as unreadably tiny fragments on the busy sweater photo. A at least keeps the LYGOM CAFE logo and cup on the pink field next to the headline (tiny, but legible). B pushes the logo to the far right edge on top of the busy photo, where it is illegible, so the brand is effectively lost.

Both share the same flaws: the symptom list is tiny and badly rewrapped ('Sore throat Headache' on one line, 'Dry cough' tacked onto 'breath') and jammed against the top edge; 'SYMPTOMS' butts into the doctor, who is cropped into a hard white box; the hashtag bar is shrunk to a floating box; and the sparkle sits alone and oversized on the right. A's CTA runs almost to the right edge, while B wraps it shorter and keeps some margin, so B is slightly less cramped.

A is mostly a uniform shrink of the original. The doctor, headline and list keep their hierarchy and proportions, but the yellow hashtag bar no longer spans the full width, and the list and yellow CTA are very small at 300x250. B breaks the design: the headline wraps awkwardly to '6 / SYMPTOMS' beside a hashtag badge, list items run together ('Sore throat Headache'), the sparkle is blown up into a huge dominant shape, and the doctor shrinks to a tiny cropped figure, which loses the key imagery.

A blows the small sparkle up into a huge white star that dominates the middle of the banner and becomes the main focal point. Its symptom list is also re-wrapped badly ('Shortness of breath Dry cough' and 'Sore throat Headache' each run two items together on one line), and the hashtag has shrunk to a tiny pill. B's list reads better and the CTA sits with it, but 'Sore throat Headache' is still merged and the text block is cramped against the edges. B also moves #FLATTENTHECURVE below the doctor as a button-like pill, which breaks the reading order, and puts an oversized star in the bottom-left corner, so B is only slightly less broken.

Both drop the bold geometric background and shrink it to a meaningless thumbnail mid-banner, with the white panel and dots stranded inside it; that loses the original's whole visual identity. A: 'OPENING JANUARY 1' is tiny and jammed against the thumbnail's right edge, and the right third is dead white space, but 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' and the 'THE MINIMALIST' pill are readable. B: 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' is shrunk to illegible fine print, the white frame spills messily past the cropped art, and the 'THE MINIMALIST' pill and date text are tiny and scattered far right, so the grouping and hierarchy are weaker.

Both break the design in the same way. The text has been pulled out of the label frame, so the frame sits empty with its orphaned divider rules floating inside. The illustration of bottles and lavender, which carried the original, has shrunk to a tiny strip with a large dead area of background below it, and 'Homemade Lotion' hangs left-of-centre in empty space. A is slightly less bad because the LAVANDER wordmark is larger and SKINCARE is readable, although 'J'adore Paris' is tiny and squeezed beside it. In B the wordmark row is smaller and SKINCARE is shrunk to near-illegible type crammed against the right edge.

A: the two hero food photos are shrunk to postage-stamp thumbnails in a bottom strip, next to empty white frames and a stray peach swatch. The ornament dividers and the pasta-pattern tile float at random, the headline is small, and the URL sits between 'Cascadia' and 'RESTAURANT', which breaks the wordmark. B: the photos are again reduced to tiny thumbnails in a top strip with empty frames, the ornaments are scattered and the pattern tile is dropped in at random. It is slightly less bad because the headline is large and leads on the left, and 'Cascadia' / 'RESTAURANT' stay grouped.

A keeps the original's centred maroon panel, with 'WE CREATE / MARKETING FUTURE', the divider and 'Join WADE team' in the right order and readable, and the photo now fills the square. Its flaws are small dark triangle notches at the panel corners and decorative marks that sit a little loosely on the panel edges. B is broken: the headline sits on the busy photo, wedged between heads and arms. The maroon panel is left as an empty block. 'Join', 'WADE' and 'team' are split into three fragments stacked down the right edge, and the decorative marks are lined up in a random row, so the CTA is lost and nothing reads as one group.

Both candidates have the same structure and the same fatal flaws. The white quote has been pulled off its red panel and placed on the light grey background, where it is almost invisible. The red/white frame is left as an empty decorative box in the middle, and the attribution is tiny white italic on grey, so it is unreadable too. The skyline is a small detached strip on the right instead of the base of the composition. B's skyline is a little larger and its panel a little narrower, but neither change fixes the contrast or the hierarchy, so the two are equivalent.

Both candidates are practically the same. The crowd illustration, which carries the original's imagery, shrinks to a thin, almost unreadable strip at the top. The quote is set very large and breaks into 12 short lines with awkward breaks ('NEVER / DOUBT THAT', 'INDEED,' left alone on its own line), and 'THOUGHTFUL' and 'CAN CHANGE' run right up to the right edge. The attribution is in a cramped block of 4 lines with an empty band below it. The two differ only by a few pixels of vertical offset, so neither is better.

Both candidates break the design the same way. The S-A-L-E letters have come out of their four circles, which now sit empty in the centre. The letters are scattered over the right half (S and A in one column, L and E far right), so the main 'SALE' message no longer reads. 'NEW YEAR SPECIAL' has moved to the top-left, away from the central focal stack, and the decorations are split into two separate clusters, losing the original's symmetry. The two differ only by a few pixels in headline size and letter position, so neither is meaningfully better.

The two candidates look essentially identical, and both break in the same ways. The S-A-L-E circle stack is pulled apart: the letters are scattered across the banner while their white circles sit empty in a tiny vertical column in the middle, so the word SALE no longer reads. The scattered letters also collide with shrunken lantern and cloud artwork, and the decorative elements are reduced to illegible specks next to an oversized 'NEW YEAR SPECIAL' block.

Both break the original's concept. The quote is pulled out of the illustrated frame and stacked one or two words per line, and the frame now shows stock placeholder text ('BEAUTY ILLUSTRATION / HAND-DRAWN ELEMENTS') where the quote used to be. The illustration is also shrunk to a small thumbnail with a big empty gap above the attribution. A is slightly less bad: its first line 'MEN ARE' breaks more naturally than B's orphaned 'MEN', it keeps the illustration a little larger, and B's 'BECAUSE' line nearly touches both canvas edges.

Both have the same failure. The green forest background covers only a narrow centre strip and the rest of the canvas is white, so the white headline ('Special Event Devoted to International Day of Forests') and subhead ('Joint celebration & Forest cleanup') disappear outside the strip and read only as fragments. The pale yellow 'March 21' and the divider rules float on white with almost no contrast, and the quote and URL body copy are missing. B frames the date between two rules and A leaves one rule stranded on the right, but neither is usable.

Both candidates are effectively the same and unusable. The background is a narrow centered strip with white dead space on both sides. The headline is far too large and runs off the background, so white text vanishes into the white sides ('Event Devo', 'ernational D'). 'March 21' sits on the pale sky with almost no contrast. The divider rule floats off into the white area, the subhead is cut off ('ration & Forest clea'), and the quote and URL are missing. B's elements sit a pixel or two to the left of A's, which makes no visible difference.

The two are almost pixel-identical, so I called it a tie. Both flip the hierarchy: the secondary line 'food & drinks' is set much larger than the 'Order online' headline. In both, 'drinks' runs over the busy kraft-box photo, a single divider rule floats on top of the boxes and the other rule is gone. The headline is also cramped on the left, leaving a dead strip in the middle. Candidate B's subtitle sits a few pixels further left, which changes nothing.

Both break the text block apart. The rules stay at left, but 'food & drinks' drifts into the middle and lands on the kraft box. In both, the subtitle is larger than the headline, so the hierarchy is inverted. A's 'Order online' is tiny and barely legible, but it stays centred between its rules, and only 'drinks' clips the box edge. B's headline is slightly larger but sits off-centre from the rules, and 'food & drinks' sits further right with '& drinks' fully on the busy box image, which is a worse collision.

A and B look pixel-identical, and both are unusable for the same reasons. The background photo is cropped into a blurry, upscaled close-up that drops the Tower Bridge imagery and the translucent panel behind the text. Dark text sits straight on a busy photo, so it is hard to read. 'FAMILY DAYS OUT IN' is cut off from its headline 'London' and pushed to the lower left, which breaks the reading order. The chevrons are blown up into a huge row of six that crowds the tagline and becomes the focal point. The layout has no common edge or grid.

A: the 'London' wordmark butts right up against the tagline, so 'London' and 'enjoy' nearly touch. 'FAMILY DAYS OUT IN' has shrunk to an illegible speck in the top right, and the busy city photo behind the text hurts contrast, though the chevrons at least sit apart on the right. B: same cramped London/tagline join and the same busy background, but the '<<<' and '>>>' chevrons collide with the ends of 'money,' and 'weekend', and the 'Family days out in' line is lost entirely, so B is worse.

Both break the design the same way. The text has been pulled out of the label frame, which is left empty apart from stray divider rules. The illustrations have shrunk to a tiny strip of icons, and the bottom third and the middle of the canvas are dead space. A squeezes 'J'adore Paris', LAVANDER and a tiny SKINCARE into one cramped header row. B makes LAVANDER bigger and slightly enlarges the illustrations, but leaves SKINCARE floating on its own, left-aligned and off the centred axis.

A: the food photos, which were the hero of the original, are now postage-stamp thumbnails in a row next to empty frame outlines, the decorative divider stroke and the pattern swatch float with no purpose, and the beige panel is gone. Its one strength is a large, clear headline. B: the same thumbnail strip with empty frames, plus a small, weak headline floating in the middle, two stray divider strokes, an isolated pattern square, and the brand block reordered so RESTAURANT sits under the URL. A edges ahead only because its headline hierarchy holds.

Both drop the original concept, where the quote sat inside a frame surrounded by illustrations. Each shrinks the illustration into a small thumbnail below the text, and that thumbnail shows a stock 'BEAUTY ILLUSTRATION / HAND DRAWN ELEMENTS' label that was not in the original, so fidelity is broken. The quote is stacked into an eight-line column with no frame. A's lines 'BECAUSE' and 'MAKEUP.' run almost to the canvas edges with no side margin. B keeps slightly more breathing room on the sides but leaves 'JUST' alone on its own line; otherwise the two are near-identical, with the attribution isolated at the bottom.

Both are unusable. The forest background is a narrow centred strip and does not fill the banner, so the white headline 'Special Event Devoted to International Day of Forests' and the subhead disappear into the white canvas on both sides. Only fragments like 'nternat', 'of For' and 'n & Forest cl' can be read, and the quote and URL are lost entirely. A is marginally less broken because 'March 21' at least sits framed between its two cream rules, though it is pale cream on white. In B, 'March 21' is smaller and one rule is stranded alone on the far right, which leaves even less structure.

A: the 'Order online' headline has shrunk to a small label, and 'food & drinks' has come apart from it and now sits on top of the kraft box photo, breaking the original rule-framed lockup; the two rules float with a large empty gap around the tiny headline. B has all of the same problems, and its headline is even smaller and nearly unreadable. 'food & drinks' is now larger than the headline, which flips the hierarchy, and it still runs across the box edge.
